seo.title: CAPIT | Every Plugged Well, One Public Record
seo.description: Explore source-linked U.S. well-plugging records from state regulators, compare states, and read exactly how records are counted. Free to use, no wallet required.

hero.headline:
Every Plugged Well.
One Public Record.
hero.description: CAPIT collects plugged-well records published by state oil and gas regulators and shows where each record came from and when it was last checked. The registry is free to use and open to everyone. Explore the national snapshot, compare states, and see exactly how records are counted.
hero.trustNote: CAPIT is an independent project of Tellus Digital, LLC. It is not a government registry and does not itself plug wells. CAPIT also has a community token on the Base network; it is separate from the registry, and you never need it to use the data. Review the risk disclosures before using any wallet or token feature.

snapshot.heading: National Snapshot
snapshot.intro: Start with the big picture: how many plugged-well records CAPIT has published, what was added recently, how states compare, and how many tokens have been minted against those records.

educationalCards.title: What Is a Plugged Well?
educationalCards.description: A well sealed with cement plugs to isolate oil, gas, and groundwater zones, cut off below ground, and recorded as plugged by the state regulator. CAPIT shows the state's original status term next to its own display label.

educationalCards.title: Why Does Plugging Wells Matter?
educationalCards.description: Plugging closes out a well's working life. It reduces the risk of gas and fluid leaks, removes surface hazards, puts skilled crews to work, and helps return land to productive use.

educationalCards.title: How Many Unplugged Wells Remain?
educationalCards.description: Estimates run from about 142,000 documented orphan wells to more than 2 million unplugged abandoned wells, depending on what is counted. See what each number measures.
educationalCards.imageAlt: Map showing inactive wells across the United States

methodologyStrip.heading: Source-linked. Time-stamped. Revision-aware.
methodologyStrip.body: Every published record carries its source agency, source record ID, retrieval date, and revision history. When a state corrects or reclassifies a record, CAPIT adds a new revision instead of overwriting the old one.
